newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends higher after breaking $26/barrel.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends higher after breaking $26/barrel.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended higher Manday after pushing past $26.00 a barrel, its highest level since January of 1991, as dealers sold heating oil in favor crude.

"There is some rotation of leadership. Heating oil had become overvalued," said Tim Evans, analyst with Pegasus Econometric Group. November crude settled up 13 cents at $25.92 a barrel after rising as high as $26.05.
"Crude is really bullish. You just don't want to stand in front of it," said Bob Yawger, a trader with E. D. & F. Man International Inc.
Traders said volume was thin, with little buying interest for refined products.
November heating oil closed down 0.43 cent a gallon to 73.63 cents while November gasoline fell only 0.02 cent a gallon at 67.92 cents.
"You have a situation where gasoline on a fundamental basis is as undervalued as the heating oil had become overvalued," said Evans.
Gasoline prices have lagged gains in the oil complex which has been in a firm uptrend in recent months propelled by heating oil prices.
Heating oil has been buoyed by record low distillate stocks.

Traders said political pressure on refiners to step up heating oil output may eventually pull distillate stocks up to more bearish levels, resulting in crude taking over price gain leadership from heat.

After a meeting last Friday between U.S. Department of Energy officials and oil executives to discuss the low distillate inventory situation, Tosco Corp and Petroleos de Venezuela's Citgo, two major refiners, said they would maximize distillate output.
Refiners are producing about 1.3 million barrels a day of heating oil and 3.6 million barrels a day of total distillates, according to the American Petroleum Institute (API).
At October 11, total distillate stocks were 17.7 million barrels below a year ago and heating oil stocks were 18 million barrels below a year ago, the API said.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
